drsBootHoldoffDesc: For this many minutes after a node boots, DRS moves no guest onto it or off it, so a cluster starting up is not rebalanced while its guests are still booting. 0 turns it off. A manual migrate is not affected.
drsHeldNode: {{node}} booted {{uptime}} ago, so DRS leaves it alone until its {{holdoff}}-minute hold-off ends.

drsRulesTable.lengthDRSAndProxmoxHA: {{length}}, DRS and Proxmox HA rules together
drsRulesTable.rulesHaveNotBeenRead: Rules have not been read yet
drsRulesTable.thisWillDeleteTheHA: This will delete the HA rule from Proxmox. This action cannot be undone.
drsRulesTable.areYouSureYouWant: Are you sure you want to delete this rule? This action cannot be undone.

drsConfigCard.howNexaraSpreadsGuestsAcross: How Nexara spreads guests across this cluster's nodes.
drsConfigCard.proxmoxNativeDynamicLoadBalancer: Proxmox native Dynamic Load Balancer is active
drsConfigCard.thisClusterSProxmoxCRS: This cluster's Proxmox CRS is auto-rebalancing HA-managed guests. Nexara DRS Automatic mode is disabled to avoid conflicting migrations; Advisory still works as a read-only second opinion. Manage the native balancer under Datacenter → Options → CRS.
drsConfigCard.disabledTurnsDRSOffAdvisory: Disabled turns DRS off. Advisory logs recommendations without acting. Automatic will live-migrate VMs.
drsConfigCard.disabledTurnsDRSOffAdvisoryNative: Disabled turns DRS off. Advisory logs recommendations without acting. Automatic will live-migrate VMs. Automatic is unavailable while Proxmox native CRS rebalancing is on.
drsConfigCard.howMuchEachResourceType: How much each resource type influences balance scoring. The two weights must sum to 1.0.
drsConfigCard.aHigherMemoryWeightMeans: A higher memory weight means DRS prioritizes evening out memory usage.
drsConfigCard.lowerValuesCauseMoreFrequent: Lower values cause more frequent migrations.
drsConfigCard.aggressiveTriggersOnSmallLoad: Aggressive: triggers on small load differences between nodes.
drsConfigCard.balancedTriggersWhenNodeLoads: Balanced: triggers when node loads diverge moderately.
drsConfigCard.conservativeOnlyTriggersOnLarge: Conservative: only triggers on large load imbalances.
drsConfigCard.evaluationIntervalMinutes: How often DRS checks cluster balance. Every {{minutes}} minutes.
drsConfigCard.evaluationIntervalSeconds: How often DRS checks cluster balance. Every {{seconds}} seconds.
drsConfigCard.containerMigrationRequiresDowntimeUnlike: Container migration requires downtime. Unlike VMs which support live migration, containers must be stopped, moved, and restarted. Only enable this if container downtime during rebalancing is acceptable.
drsConfigCard.drsMayThenMigrateA: DRS may then migrate a Veeam worker appliance mid-backup, which fails the job running on it and leaves nothing behind but a failed session. Veeam's guests are still counted toward node load either way.

drsHistoryTable.whatDRSMovedOrRecommended: What DRS moved or recommended, newest first

drsEvaluateButton.scoreTheNodesNowAnd: Score the nodes now and see what DRS would move. Nothing is migrated unless the mode is Automatic.
drsEvaluateButton.evaluationSkippedProxmoxNativeCRS: Evaluation skipped: Proxmox native CRS active
drsEvaluateButton.proxmoxNativeCRSAutoRebalance: Proxmox native CRS auto-rebalance is enabled on this cluster, so Nexara automatic migrations are paused. Switch DRS to Advisory mode to generate recommendations without migrating.
drsEvaluateButton.loadVarianceImbalanceIsWithin: Load variance ({{imbalance}}) is within the configured threshold ({{threshold}}). No migrations needed.
drsEvaluateButton.loadVarianceImbalanceExceedsThe: Load variance ({{imbalance}}) exceeds the threshold ({{threshold}}), but no single VM migration would improve the balance. This typically happens when nodes have very few VMs or when workloads are too large relative to the load difference: moving any one VM would overshoot and make things worse.
drsEvaluateButton.automaticModeAnEvaluationHas: Automatic mode: an evaluation has been queued. The scheduler re-plans against live cluster state on its next pass (usually within a minute) and executes what it finds then, so the moves below are the plan as of now and may differ. Results appear in DRS history.

noNodesFound: No nodes found for this cluster.
acceptNewNameDescription: Nexara recorded this cluster as {{recorded}}, and its API URL now reaches a cluster named {{reported}}. Accept only if the cluster was renamed, or this entry was pointed at {{reported}} on purpose. Nexara then removes the nodes of {{recorded}} that {{reported}} does not list, with their metrics and settings in Nexara.
acceptNewNameFailed: Nexara could not accept the name.
savedButUnreachable: Saved cluster {{name}}, but Nexara could not reach it: {{message}}. Check the API URL and the token.

editClusterDialog.addressMoved: This cluster is moving to a new address, so it needs the token secret again — the stored one is only ever sent to the address it was saved for.
editClusterDialog.sshClearedNotice: Node addresses are learned from this API, so the stored SSH credential and every pinned host key were entrusted to machines this cluster is leaving. Saving clears both. Re-enter the credential and re-pin each node before the next rolling update.
editClusterDialog.tokenSecretReenter: Re-enter the token secret for the new address
editClusterDialog.selfSignedDescription: The server at <url>{{url}}</url> uses a self-signed certificate. Verify this fingerprint matches your Proxmox host before accepting.
editClusterDialog.fingerprintChanged: This fingerprint differs from the currently stored fingerprint. The server certificate has changed.
editClusterDialog.acceptFingerprint: I have verified this fingerprint and trust this certificate
editClusterDialog.trustedDescription: The server at <url>{{url}}</url> has a valid certificate signed by a trusted CA.
editClusterDialog.fingerprintUpdatedOnSave: The fingerprint will be updated on save.
